subject.title: [Feature] Queue prompts when API limits prevent an immediate response

question: Should OpenClaw add a core SQLite-backed capacity-wait queue for prompts blocked by provider/model API limits, and how should that coordinate with the existing open queue and cooldown PRs?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug patch because it changes persistent runtime state, provider retry semantics, user-visible wait state, and how partial PRs should be adopted or replaced.

options.title: Sponsor Durable Capacity-Wait Queue
options.body: Design the queue as core SQLite state with replay and visibility semantics, then land or replace related PR slices only where they fit that design.

options.title: Narrow To Followup Restart Persistence
options.body: Treat provider-limit auto-replay as separate future work and only pursue durable followup queues across restart first.

options.title: Keep Cooldown Suspension Only
options.body: Accept cooldown copy and session suspension as intended behavior and close the broader automatic replay direction later with an explicit product decision.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Durable Capacity-Wait Queue
recommendation.body: Design the queue as core SQLite state with replay and visibility semantics, then land or replace related PR slices only where they fit that design.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available owner signal because recent history places steipete on both the queue runtime and model-fallback/session-suspension paths.
